(2) The perspective shifts outdoors where the same hand holds the miniature mailbox up against a full-sized real red Japanese post box. The background shows a brick building and green bushes in natural daylight. (3) Back indoors, the miniature mailbox is placed between two Maruko-chan dolls. The hand removes the top lid of the mailbox to reveal a slot, then shows a second lid variant, demonstrating a modular feature on the white tabletop. (4) The camera zooms in on the front of the miniature mailbox, showing highly detailed stickers that replicate the text and collection times of a real Japanese post box with sharp focus and high contrast. (5) A hand inserts another tiny envelope into the left slot of the miniature mailbox, emphasizing the functional open-slot design against the clean white background. (6) The hand pulls open the side door of the red miniature mailbox, mimicking the action of a postal worker. Inside the compartment, several tiny paper envelopes are clustered together. (7) A 100-yen coin is held above the mailbox and dropped into the top slot, revealing the object's secondary function as a piggy bank while the Maruko-chan figures watch from the sides. (8) The hand tilts the mailbox to show the interior through the open side door as envelopes and coins sit inside. (9) The miniature is held again in front of the real mailbox outdoors, shifting the background to a street view with a high-angle tilt. (10) A pink graphic outro screen appears with the 'Japanuts' logo, social media handles for Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube, and a website URL.
